payload.name: Compound Activity Retrieval with Constraint Omission
payload.description: Use when a question asks for an activity or pastime combining a person's enjoyment with another condition (indoor, pet, another person), and initial results only match one side of the condition.
content: After the first search, run at least one follow-up query using only enjoyment/hobby terms ('hobby', 'enjoys', 'interested in', 'started', 'likes to') and deliberately omit all additional-constraint keywords such as indoor, pet, or the other person.
Include memory kinds preference, event, and plan in these follow-ups; a hobby can be stored as a routine, plan, or preference without mentioning the extra condition.

If a retrieved hobby can reasonably satisfy the extra condition (e.g., an indoor-friendly hobby or a hobby that can involve a pet), treat that as the best candidate; otherwise answer from the best available evidence and do not invent connections.
Stop after one such follow-up and one combination check; avoid further expansion.

solves: When a question asks for an activity that a person would enjoy while also satisfying another condition, such as being indoors, involving a pet, or pleasing someone else, retrieval often over-anchors on the extra condition and misses the person's stored hobby or preference that is recorded without mentioning that condition.
